title: Jev in-context casebooks: test examples before you trust them
description: Customize Jev with labelled examples instead of training: define answers, compare retrieved and full casebooks without leakage, and version each casebook.

source.title: How to Make In-Context Learning Work with Jev

guide_authors.name: Appit Studio
guide_authors.role: Original editorial guide; AI-assisted research, drafting and offline verification

image.alt: Four steps for in-context examples with Jev: define each answer, compare no examples with retrieved examples from a training-only pool, test a full casebook if it fits, and version the casebook with a separate test set

connections.step: See a harness that varies the number of labelled examples in Jev's state and compares against trained baselines
connections.why: Jev IDS puts the record under test and a set of labelled pool examples into one request's state, sweeps examples per category across seeds, and scores the same splits with a Random Forest and an Isolation Forest. That is the example-count and trained-baseline comparison the source recommends, in a different domain. David Bressler does not name it.
connections.limitations: MIT Python research benchmark on network-flow records (NSL-KDD), not text classification; Python 3.13+ and a TypeSafe key for live runs, which send flow features to TypeSafe and are billed. Examples are drawn at random per category rather than retrieved. Source inspected only; not executed. Its results are the maintainer's.

verification.source: Read the complete X article and its companion, One Model, a Different Rulebook for Every Customer, through the X API article fields on 2026-10-23, including the article's JSON request example. Both disclose that Eventum is an official TypeSafe technology partner and that TypeSafe's CTO advises Eventum. The linked Eventum write-up, TypeSafe docs and decision-model evaluation article resolve. Source images not reused; original CC0 diagram created.
verification.offline: Checked current TypeSafe Choice, models and long-context docs: 64k per-request and 32k per-question limits by default, 262k for both with the TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context header, which the docs describe as slower and less accurate. Ran the guide's casebook builder with a small TF-IDF retriever on fixture records: train and test groups were disjoint, the target never appeared among its own examples, and a tight token budget reduced the examples sent and reported the shortfall. Inspected Jev IDS at 6aa5ac4570db1d6d9b88f769f7d16c1cd2c3784a: request construction and the example-count and seed options.
verification.live: No Jev inference, retrieval over a real dataset, full-casebook or long-context request, selector stage, fine-tuning comparison, accuracy, calibration or cost measurement. Every result quoted is Eventum's.
verification.review: AI-assisted editorial review; no human reviewer. No keyword tool or Search Console data was consulted. No existing guide covers in-context examples, casebooks or per-customer policies for Jev; the text-to-columns and content-triage guides use fixed instructions without examples.

faqs.question: Can Jev be fine-tuned on my labels?
faqs.answer: No. TypeSafe's models page says Jev is not fine-tuned or LoRA-adapted with customer data and the same weights serve every account. You customize it through the request: state, instructions, criteria and, as this guide shows, labelled examples placed in the state.

faqs.question: How many examples should I put in a Jev request?
faqs.answer: Start with none and with up to 32 retrieved examples, and compare them on a development split. In the source, 32 retrieved examples helped on all four tasks, while thousands of random examples sometimes did worse. A full casebook won on banking intents but cost far more.

faqs.question: Do I need long context for a full casebook?
faqs.answer: Only if it exceeds the default limits of 64k tokens per request and 32k per question. The long-context header raises both to 262k, and TypeSafe says such requests are slower and less accurate. Log the setting so you know which mode you evaluated.

faqs.question: How do I stop test labels leaking into the examples?
faqs.answer: Split records into training, development and test pools before building the retrieval index, keep related documents and near-duplicates in one pool, and build the index from the training pool only. A test case must never retrieve itself or a copy of itself.

faqs.question: Is a better casebook enough to automate decisions?
faqs.answer: No. In the source, neither highlighted selector found any set of answers that met a 1 percent error target on 200 calibration cases. Fit acceptance thresholds on separate data and report when no useful operating point exists.

faqs.question: When is fine-tuning a separate model the better choice?
faqs.answer: When the task is stable, high-volume and well labelled. In the source a fine-tuned MiniLM scored 92.35 percent on Emotion against 76.00 percent for the Jev selector. Casebooks matter most when boundaries differ by customer or change often.
